items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: In fact they were my buddies, especially David and Michael and Grover became a dear friend.

ctx.x: Was there competition, friendly or not, between the saxophone players especially because if any wind instrument is going to get a gig playing solos it’s probably going to be a saxophone. So you have Ernie Watts and Plas Johnson and people at that level. Did you run into these other players and sort of like, “So what have you been doing lately? Who did you play with?”

Not at all. It was not like that at all. No. No. No. Look we were a fraternity of very lucky musicians who managed to get into this very heady department of the music business. So we were thrilled to be there. I considered them fellow travelers, fellow musicians who I respected and admired. But you know also there were others at the time, in addition to Ernie and Plas, there was David Sanborn, there was Michael Brecker, there was Grover Washington. Now those guys pretty much — I’m sure there are other people I’m…
